title: UART transmitter (8N1)
spec: A UART transmitter that sends 8-bit words as frames of one start bit, eight data bits, and one stop bit, with one rising-edge clock clk. Each bit lasts CLKS_PER_BIT clock cycles; a cycle is the interval between two consecutive rising edges. tx and busy are registered outputs that change only at rising edges.
rst is a synchronous active-high reset: at a rising edge with rst high, the transmitter becomes idle: tx becomes 1 and busy becomes 0.

While idle, tx is 1 and busy is 0. At a rising edge without reset where busy is low and start is high, the transmitter accepts data (sampled at that edge) and starts a frame. start is ignored at edges where busy is high.

During a frame, starting right after the accepting edge: tx is 0 for CLKS_PER_BIT cycles (the start bit), then data bit 0, data bit 1, and so on up to data bit 7 for CLKS_PER_BIT cycles each (least significant bit first), then 1 for CLKS_PER_BIT cycles (the stop bit). busy is high for the whole frame, 10 times CLKS_PER_BIT cycles, and goes low together with the end of the stop bit, when the transmitter is idle again.
